sections.title: Introduction
body: An Array is a linear data structure that stores elements in contiguous memory locations.
All elements in an array are of the same data type.
Each element can be accessed directly using its index.
Arrays provide fast access to elements but have fixed size in most languages.

sections.title: Properties
body: Stores elements in contiguous memory locations.
Indexing usually starts from 0 in most programming languages.
All elements are of the same data type.
Size of array is fixed at the time of creation.

sections.title: Operations
body: - Insert at a specific index by shifting elements.
- Delete an element by shifting remaining elements.
- Visit each element one by one using a loop.

sections.title: Traversal Techniques
body: Sequential Traversal: Access elements from start to end.
Reverse Traversal: Access elements from end to start.
Index-based Traversal: Access using index values.
Using Iterators: Used in languages like Java and C++.

sections.title: Applications
body: Used to store and process lists of data.
Used in searching and sorting algorithms.
Used in implementing other data structures like stacks and queues.

sections.title: Disadvantages
body: Fixed size (cannot grow dynamically in static arrays).
Wastage of memory if size is not fully used.
